Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 90, verses 1–4:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Balad (The City), because it opens with God's oath by the city, which is Makkah.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• A refutation of the polytheists who were deceived by their strength, so they obstinately rejected the truth and denied the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and spent their wealth in boasting and vainglory. It also reminds them of God's power over them and the completeness of His knowledge of them, and rebukes them for neglecting to thank God for His blessings upon them. It reminds people of the hardships that lie before them in the Hereafter, which they cannot pass through except by faith and righteous deeds, and it distinguishes between the believers and the disbelievers on that Day by explaining the destiny of the happy and the destiny of the wretched.

[Tafsir]

God swears by this sacred city, which is "Makkah," and you, O Prophet, are permitted in this "sacred city" to do whatever you wish in it, though it was made lawful for him only for an hour of a day. In the verse there is good news for the Prophet (ﷺ) of the conquest of "Makkah" at his hands, and its being made lawful for him in fighting. And He swears by the father of mankind, who is Adam (peace be upon him), and what came forth from him of offspring: indeed, We created man in hardship and toil, struggling through the trials of this world.

Surah 90 (al-Balad), verse 13:

Meaning: It is freeing a believing slave from bondage.

Translation of the commentary:

It is freeing a believing slave from the bondage of slavery.

Or feeding, on a day of severe hunger, an orphan whose father has died while he was young, from among one's relatives, combining the merit of charity with the maintaining of family ties; or a destitute poor man who has nothing at all.

Then he was among those who, in addition to doing the good deeds mentioned, sincerely believed in God, and who enjoined one another to patience in obedience to God and in refraining from His disobedience, and enjoined one another to show mercy to creation.
The people who do these deeds are the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), those who will be taken on the Day of Resurrection toward the right, into Paradise.
"Those who disbelieved in the Qur'an are the ones who will be seized on the Day of Resurrection and taken to the Fire on the left."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 90, verse 20:

Their recompense is the Fire (Jahannam), sealed shut and closed over them.
